title: Scoring live traffic: sampling what to grade, and the cost of grading it

videos.script: Rules see the form of a reply. Whether it answers the question needs something that reads. {{judge}} So a second model grades the first. Here it is the same small model, which is the judge a team has when it has one. On live traffic there is no answer key, so it can judge relevance and faithfulness, and not correctness. {{criteria}} Graded on everything, the week says forty-three percent before the release and thirty-four after. That took twenty-five minutes of this machine, and the judge failed every refusal, the right ones too. {{all}} A tenth of the traffic, chosen at random, is twenty-three replies, and its intervals cover most of the scale. {{uniform}} The replies customers doubted say almost nothing passes. True of those replies, and nothing like the week. {{targeted}} How sure a sample is depends on how many replies it holds, not on the size of the traffic. Even the whole week cannot prove the release did harm. {{sizes}} And every judgement has a price. Here, a third more than the reply cost to write, per criterion. {{cost}} A sample is how a team grades every day and still pays for it. {{end}}
